pairs.subject: mcp-tools
pairs.evidence: scripts/ci/mcp-gate-parity.mjs:41 This context's MCP gate checks after the fact that three hand-copied lists of the gated tool names agree (what is advertised, what dispatch allows, and what gets a refusal); the standard's server-composition rule says listing and dispatch should be read from one registry, and the gate's own header admits that single authority does not exist yet.

techniques.evidence: scripts/ci/mcp-gate-parity.mjs:41 Three hand-maintained copies of the gated vocabulary (verified in crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs: 290/476 list blocks, guarded arms 746-754, refusal arm 755). The standard names parallel lists as the anti-pattern; this gate is a floor under the gap, not a fix for it.

scripts/ci/mcp-gate-parity.mjs:210 The operator switch hides whole tool groups. The gate checks both directions (advertised vs guarded dispatch, gated vs refusal arm), and a call to a hidden tool must get a refusal that names the setting that restores it. That is the 'paid-for second authority' plus the 'refusal names the switch' rule.

pairs.registryProposal: catalog-projection-modes allows a second authority only when an outside cap on catalog size forces it. It has no rule for a second authority that exists for no such reason and is held together by a build-time parity check. Please state whether a CI parity gate counts as the bidirectional completeness assertions 'that run wherever the artifact runs', or only as a temporary floor.
